title: Withholding & the W-4
description: The prepayment on the paycheck, the form that sets it, and the refund that is not a prize.
wolfLine: A refund is your money coming home late.

withholding.definition: Tax your employer takes out of each paycheck and sends to the IRS in your name. It is a prepayment, not a separate extra tax.
withholding.example: A $2,620 income-tax bill and $3,000 withheld means a $380 refund.

w-4.definition: The form you give your employer so it knows how much federal income tax to withhold. You can change it when a job, a marriage, or a second paycheck changes the picture.
w-4.example: Chris has two jobs. Each W-4 was filled out as if it were his only job, so too little was withheld.

lessons.title: What Withholding Is
lessons.summary: The IRS is already collecting during the year.

steps.title: A prepayment
steps.body:
[[Withholding]] is federal income tax taken from the paycheck. It is credited against the bill you saw in the last unit.

It is not [[FICA]]. FICA is Social Security and Medicare. A W-4 changes the income-tax withholding, not the FICA rate.

steps.prompt: What is withholding?
choices: Income tax your employer sends ahead, in your name
steps.explain: It is your money, parked with the IRS until the return sorts it out.

steps.prompt: The tax is $2,620 and withholding is $3,000. How much comes back?
The tax is $2,620 and withholding is $2,000. How much do you still owe?
Withholding is a second tax on top of the income tax.
steps.explain: It is the income tax, paid early. The return compares it with the real bill.

lessons.title: When to Update the W-4
lessons.summary: A life change is a form, not a hope.

steps.title: The form is yours
steps.body:
A [[W-4|w-4]] tells the employer how much federal income tax to withhold. Fill a new one when you marry, have a child, add a job, or your refund or your bill keeps surprising you.

The IRS withholding estimator on irs.gov is the tool. This lesson does not fill the form for you.

steps.prompt: Which change is a reason to look at the W-4 again?
choices: Your commute is one block shorter
steps.explain: A second paycheck changes the tax. The estimator is built for that.

steps.prompt: A W-4 changes the FICA rate.
steps.explain: FICA is set by law. The W-4 changes income-tax withholding.

steps.prompt: Where is the careful place to estimate a new W-4?
choices: Last year’s refund, with no new numbers
steps.explain: The estimator uses your pay, your other job, and your filing status.

steps.prompt: You give the W-4 to your ___.
steps.explain: The employer is who withholds. The IRS is who receives it.

lessons.title: Refund or a Bill
lessons.summary: Both are your money. The timing is the difference.

steps.title: A refund is not a prize
steps.body:
A refund means withholding was larger than the tax. A bill means it was smaller. The tax can be the same either way.

On a **$2,620** tax, withholding of **$3,000** refunds **$380**. Withholding of **$2,200** means you owe **$420**.

steps.prompt: Tax $2,620, withholding $2,200. How much do you owe?
How much more was withheld in the $3,000 case than in the $2,200 case?
What is a refund?
steps.explain: You paid $3,000 toward a $2,620 bill. The $380 was always yours.

steps.prompt: Owing at filing time means the return was done wrong.
steps.explain: It means withholding was short of the bill. The return can still be right.

lessons.title: The IRS Estimator
lessons.summary: Use the official one when two numbers disagree.

steps.title: Bring the paystubs
steps.body:
The IRS withholding estimator asks for pay, how often you are paid, other jobs, and credits. It suggests a [[W-4|w-4]].

A guess that “a refund is always good” skips the tool. A **$1,200** refund on a **$2,620** tax means **$3,820** was withheld. That is **$1,200** you did not have during the year.

steps.prompt: The tax is $2,620 and the refund is $1,200. How much was withheld?
How much more is that than a withholding of $2,620, which would refund $0 of income tax?
steps.explain: $3,820 − $2,620 = $1,200. A $0 refund here means withholding matched the tax.

steps.prompt: What should you type into the estimator?
choices: The pay on your stubs, including a second job
The refund you wish you could have
steps.explain: The tool is only as good as the pay you enter.

steps.prompt: A big refund is proof the estimator is required by law.
steps.explain: The estimator is a tool. A big refund is a clue that withholding was high, not a legal duty to use one website.

lessons.title: Two Jobs
lessons.summary: Each job may withhold as if it were the only one.

steps.title: The brackets do not know about each other
steps.body:
Job A pays **$30,000** and withholds **$1,500**. Job B pays **$20,000** and withholds **$800**. Together the wages are **$50,000** and the withholding is **$2,300**.

Each [[W-4|w-4]] may assume it is the only job, so each one aims at the low brackets. The combined taxable income does not.

steps.prompt: What are the two jobs’ wages together?
What is the withholding from both jobs?
Single, 2026. Taxable income on $50,000 is $33,900. The tax is $1,240 plus 12% of $21,500, which is $3,820. How much is still unpaid?
Two small withholdings add up to the same result as one W-4 that knows about both jobs.
steps.explain: Each job may withhold too little because it cannot see the other paycheck.

lessons.title: A W-4’s Extra Line
lessons.summary: The extra box is a dollar amount, not a feeling.

steps.title: Twenty-six paychecks
steps.body:
This [[W-4|w-4]] asks the employer to withhold an extra **$40** each paycheck. There are **26** paychecks. That extra is **$1,040** for the year.

It sits on top of the **$2,200** the employer was already withholding.

lines.label: Federal income tax withheld before the extra

steps.prompt: What is $40 extra across 26 paychecks?

lines.label: Federal income tax withheld before the extra

steps.prompt: What is total federal income tax withheld on this page?
Why would someone add the extra $40?
choices: A second job is not withholding enough
steps.explain: The extra line is how you catch up when the ordinary withholding is short.

steps.prompt: The extra $40 is paid once a year.
steps.explain: It is per paycheck. Twenty-six of them make $1,040.

lessons.title: A Refund Is a 0% Loan
lessons.summary: The bigger refund is the same tax, paid earlier.

steps.context: Both pages have the same **$2,620** tax. The large refund is your money, returned later, with no interest.
steps.prompt: How much is the refund when $4,000 was withheld?
How much is the refund when $2,800 was withheld?
How much more stayed out of the paychecks on the $4,000 page?
The tax is the same. Which page leaves more money in the paychecks during the year?
choices: They leave the same amount in the paychecks
why: The extra $1,200 comes back only as a refund.
steps.explain: The $4,000 page withholds $1,200 more and refunds that $1,200 later.

steps.prompt: The $1,380 refund is interest the IRS pays you for waiting.
steps.explain: It is your own $1,200 of extra withholding, plus the smaller refund on the other page. No interest is added here.

lessons.title: Chris Has Two Jobs
lessons.summary: The shortfall is the tax minus what both jobs sent.

story.title: Chris has two jobs
story.body:
Chris is 24 and works two jobs. One pays **$30,000** and withholds **$1,500** of federal income tax. The other pays **$20,000** and withholds **$800**.

Together that is **$50,000** of wages and **$2,300** withheld. He is single. The 2026 [[standard deduction]] leaves taxable income of **$33,900**, and the tax is **$3,820**.

He owes **$1,520**. Each [[W-4|w-4]] was filled out as if it were the only job. The IRS estimator is the next step, not a bigger hope for a refund.

steps.prompt: How much did both jobs withhold?
His tax is $3,820. How much does he still owe?
What is his taxable income on $50,000 of wages?
What is the useful fix before next April?
choices: A new W-4, checked with the IRS estimator
Ignore the second job on both forms
steps.explain: The estimator can see both jobs. The old forms could not.

steps.prompt: Chris owes $1,520 because the 12% bracket taxed his first dollar.
steps.explain: The first $12,400 was still taxed at 10%. He owes because $2,300 was withheld toward a $3,820 bill.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Withholding & the W-4
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: Tax is $1,800 and withholding is $1,250. How much is still owed?
A second job starts in June. What should you revisit?
choices: The W-4, with the IRS estimator
steps.explain: The new paycheck changes the withholding math.

steps.prompt: A larger refund means you paid less tax.
steps.explain: It means more tax was prepaid. The bill is a separate number.

steps.prompt: An extra $25 is withheld for 24 paychecks. How much is that for the year?
